name: Pathwise
description: A bright, game-like learning path: short lessons as round nodes on a winding path, a chunky progress bar over every lesson, quick checks between explanations, lessons that open one after another, and a unit test at the end.
modelledOn: A gamified language- and maths-learning app
features: Preset: Learning path — lessons as round nodes on a winding path
Chunky 16px progress bar over every lesson, in the success green
Lessons open one after another (linear order), with a padlock on the rest
Quick checks between explanations; a checkpoint quiz and a unit test
Answers shown after every attempt — it is practice, not an exam
Saturated palette, rounded heavy Nunito, chunky 16px buttons on a raised 3D edge
Zero custom CSS — every detail is a theme setting

authors.name: Sam Okafor
authors.bio: Sam has taught fractions to ten-year-olds and to their parents, and prefers pizza to pie charts.

metadata.subtitle: Short, playful lessons that take you from “what is a fraction?” to adding them in your head.
metadata.coverAlt: A winding path of round lesson nodes, three of them completed

modules.name: Unit 1 · Meet fractions
modules.description: What a fraction is, and where it sits.

pages.title: What is a fraction?

fields.objectives: Name the numerator and the denominator

pages.markdown:
A fraction is a number that describes **part of a whole**.

Cut a pizza into 4 equal slices and eat 1. You ate **1/4** of the pizza.

- The bottom number (the **denominator**) says how many equal parts the whole is cut into.
- The top number (the **numerator**) says how many of those parts you have.

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Fractions on a number line

fields.objectives: Place a fraction on a number line

pages.markdown:
Between 0 and 1 on a number line, cut the gap into equal steps. Each step is one part.

With 3 steps, the marks are **1/3**, **2/3** and **3/3** — and 3/3 is the same as 1.

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Compare fractions

fields.objectives: Compare fractions with a common numerator or denominator

pages.markdown:
When the denominators match, the bigger numerator wins: **3/8 > 1/8**.

When the numerators match, the **smaller** denominator wins, because the pieces are bigger: **1/3 > 1/5**.

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Equivalent fractions
pages.markdown:
**1/2**, **2/4** and **4/8** look different but cover the same amount.

Multiply (or divide) the top and bottom by the same number and you get an equivalent fraction.

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Simplify fractions
pages.markdown:
To simplify, divide the top and bottom by the biggest number that divides both.

**6/9** → both divide by 3 → **2/3**.

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Common denominators

fields.objectives: Rewrite two fractions over a common denominator

pages.markdown:
To compare 2/3 and 3/4, rewrite both with the **same** denominator.

12 is a multiple of 3 and 4: **2/3 = 8/12** and **3/4 = 9/12**. Now compare the tops: 3/4 is bigger.

modules.name: Unit 3 · Add and subtract
modules.description: Putting fractions together and taking them apart.

pages.title: Add fractions with like denominators

fields.objectives: Add fractions with the same denominator

pages.markdown:
Same denominator? Add the tops and keep the bottom.

**2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7**

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Add fractions with unlike denominators
pages.markdown:
Different denominators? Find a common denominator first.

**1/2 + 1/3** → **3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6**

:::quiz{data=""}:::

pages.title: Subtract fractions

fields.objectives: Subtract fractions and simplify the answer

pages.markdown:
Subtracting works the same way: common denominator, then subtract the tops.

**5/6 − 1/3** → **5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2**
